1. MET — no git2 type is named outside src/vcs/git/. The five remaining mentions (vcs/mod.rs, vcs/discover.rs, vcs/repo.rs) are all doc comments explaining the boundary.

Both children closed. Success Criteria verified against merged code:

1. MET — 'work that exists nowhere else cannot be destroyed by a single keystroke'. Gate::Enter returns true only on the safe shape; the guarded shapes are Gate::Override (a distinct X key, jj only, where jj undo can restore) and Gate::Phrase (typing the space's own name, git, where loss is permanent). Enter is inert in both, deliberately, because it is the reflex key that dismisses every other dialog. D no longer skips the guard, only the question. The one-keystroke path survives only where nothing would be lost, pinned by force_delete_skips_the_dialog_only_when_nothing_would_be_lost.

2. MET — 'states what will be lost in concrete terms'. The dialog names a counted figure ('1 uncommitted file (modified, staged or untracked)'), lists what is removed besides the directory, and states for jj that the bookmark survives. All wording is derived from src/vcs/delete.rs, the same source that decides the gate, so prose cannot drift from the safety decision.

Beyond the criteria, shanti-7q6.2 fixed a real hole found in passing: the old dirty check excluded untracked files, so a worktree holding only untracked work read as clean and deleted on one Enter.
